KOKO DELIVERS EMOTIONAL VALEDICTORY SPEECH, RECALLS SENATE JOURNEY AND LEGACY

Outgoing Senate Minority Leader Koko Pimentel on Wednesday, June 11, delivered his valedictory speech, marking the end of his 13-year tenure in the Senate with gratitude, reflection, and calls for continued service to the Filipino people.

In a heartfelt address, Pimentel recounted how his journey to the Senate began unconventionally through an electoral protest. He expressed gratitude to those who voted to allow him to assume his seat in August 2011. He named Sen. Pia Cayetano, outgoing Sen. Bong Revilla, Senator-elect Kiko Pangilinan, former Sen. Gringo Honasan, and Sen. Lito Lapid, as well as retired Supreme Court justices Antonio Carpio, Teresita Leonardo-De Castro, and Arturo Brion, who played key roles in his entry.

"I was never a valedictorian," Pimentel quipped, "but I still get to deliver a valedictory speech." Reflecting on his introverted nature, he added, "Who would have predicted or who would have thought that this would happen to an introvert person like me?"

He looked back on his time as Senate President from 2016 to 2018, crediting Sen. Loren Legarda for encouraging him to take on the role once held by his father, the late Senate President Nene Pimentel. During his leadership, he cited landmark laws he helped pass, including free college tuition, free irrigation, wage hikes for public servants, the TRAIN Law, and the Mental Health Act, among others.

Pimentel also acknowledged his stint as Minority Leader, joking that it forced him to read "almost all" of the majority's bills. He expressed gratitude to Senate Deputy Minority Leader Risa Hontiveros, his sole companion in the minority bloc.

He reiterated his advocacy for constitutional reforms such as federalism, the abolition of travel tax, and the modernization of the health and education systems. He also called for renewed attention to unaddressed proposals, including the creation of a hospital for senior citizens and the integration of computer programming into basic education.

Calling the Senate a place for "courageous discourse," Pimentel thanked his colleagues, staff, and even his critics, saying, "Kung meron pong nasaktan sa aking mga kilos, nasabi, actions or na-file, I beg for your understanding. In the passage of time you will find it in your heart to forgive me."

As he concluded, Pimentel said his time in public office may be ending, but his service would continue as a lawyer and private citizen. He left the chamber with one final wish: "May the laws you pass rescue the poor and helpless and deliver them from the grasp of evil people, as it is written in Psalm 82:4"

"It has been the honor of my life to serve you as Senator of the Republic of the Philippines," he said. "Maraming maraming salamat po sa Sambayang Pilipinas."
